# Tried 5 Best Interview Practice Tools — My Honest Review

[![Jack Cole](https://miro.medium.com/v2/da:true/resize:fill:32:32/0*aBj8RnlIGNe62LU2)](https://medium.com/@masonallen.official?source=post_page---byline--a1cb395dfb1a---------------------------------------)

Last year, I made a decision that genuinely scared me, I applied for a **Sr. Software Development Engineer role at Amazon**. It was the kind of opportunity where your entire career feels like it’s on the line, and with layoffs happening everywhere, taking this leap felt even more intimidating

Amazon doesn’t just check if you can code. They test how deeply you understand every decision you’ve ever made. They challenge your communication under pressure, your ownership of hard problems, and your ability to stay calm when the stakes are high. Even seasoned engineers struggle.

I genuinely believed I was ready. I had solved hundreds of DSA problems, watched countless YouTube mock interviews, and practiced system design so much that I could sketch architectures from memory. But the moment I actually spoke in a practice interview, everything changed. My thoughts felt scattered, my answers lost structure, and all that preparation suddenly didn’t sound as good out loud as it did in my head.

So I shifted my strategy. Instead of just studying in silence, I started training for the real environment. I looked for interview practice tools that could simulate pressure, give actionable feedback, and help me strengthen the one thing I was struggling with the most, clear communication under stress. I wanted something that corrected me when I hesitated, helped me structure tough questions, and pushed me to perform like it was the actual interview day.

So in this guide, I’m sharing my honest experience using 5 interview practice tools, what worked, what didn’t, and which ones are actually worth your time.

Here is the summary of my whole review

**FinalRound AI (⭐ 4.9/5)** : The only tool that actually felt like a real interview for me. Realistic interviewer avatars, easy setup, and questions that were clearly based on my own experience, not random templates.

Highlights: Very realistic mock interview flow, strong use of your resume/background, best suited if you seriously want to simulate a high-stakes interview and fix your communication under pressure.

**Interview Warmup by Google (⭐ 3.7/5):** More like a basic learning hub than an interview simulator. Good if you want to brush up on fundamentals, not great if you’re already deep into prep and want real mock interviews.

Highlights: Simple to get started, decent for revising basics, but limited customization and no real “interview-like” experience once you’re ready for serious practice.

**Exponent / Pramp (⭐ 3.4/5)** : Built more around practicing with people than with AI. Useful if you want peer or expert-led mock interviews, but not what I was looking for when I just wanted to jump into an AI-led, on-demand session.

Highlights: Multiple practice modes (friend, peers, experts), solid for human mock interviews, but the flow is confusing and not ideal if you just want a clean, solo AI interview experience.

**Interviews Chat (⭐ 2.8/5)** : Clearly positioned as an interview prep platform, but the actual experience didn’t click for me. The resume copy-paste step and awkward avatar made it feel more like a demo than a serious mock interview tool.

Highlights: Focused on interview prep, tries to use your resume and JD, but clunky input, weird lip-sync avatar, and no clear value from the “face” on screen made it hard for me to take it seriously.

**Lockedin AI (⭐ 2.5/5):** So many tools and options that I couldn’t quickly figure out how to just start an AI mock interview. I somehow ended up acting like the interviewer myself, which is the opposite of what I wanted.

Highlights: Looks powerful on paper with multiple modules, but confusing UX, unclear direction, and no straightforward “start mock interview” flow meant I dropped it fast. Might be good if you dig into it, but it definitely didn’t work for me.

**Disclaimer:** This review is based on my personal experience using each tool. Features may change in future.

## 1\. FinalRound AI (4.9/5)

When I opened the FinalRound AI Mock Interview page, I genuinely had to pause for a moment , the variety of realistic interviewer avatars actually surprised me. You can choose who interviews you based on the role or vibe you want to practice with, which makes the whole experience feel much more like a real interview instead of just another automated Q&A tool.

Press enter or click to view image in full size

![](https://miro.medium.com/v2/resize:fit:700/1*QPLJvQ9npR3kCaHuHgptzg.png)

I went with the “Standard Interviewer” since I was using the trial version,

Press enter or click to view image in full size

![](https://miro.medium.com/v2/resize:fit:700/1*QqOJlrNBuRV6CIeyVCzHjg.png)

I filled in all my details and launched the session

Press enter or click to view image in full size

![](https://miro.medium.com/v2/resize:fit:700/1*HsGSiXBOtwFXjsY06Dzf_g.png)

It was pretty easy to start with and it was very realistic by the way

Press enter or click to view image in full size

![](https://miro.medium.com/v2/resize:fit:700/1*0YJivW-qjxlmdt6VYYcCCw.png)

I liked how it felt like a real interview and was able to ask me questions based on my experiences.

**Pros**

- It feels like a _real_ interview rather than a quiz app because of the realistic interviewer avatars you can pick based on role or vibe.
- Final Round AI’s mock interview tool puts you in a “high-stakes” environment, which is closer to what you’ll feel in an Amazon-style interview or any other big MNC interview.
- Designed specifically for mock interviews, not generic learning, so the whole flow is aligned with actual interview prep.
- Great fit for people who want to practice communication under pressure, not just solve questions in their head.
- When you land on the mock interview page, the realistic interviewer avatars instantly make it feel different from usual “type your answer in a box” tools.
- You can actually choose _who_ interviews you based on role or vibe, which makes the whole thing feel closer to a real interview instead of a generic AI chat.
- Getting started was smooth: I just filled in my details, launched the session, and I was in the interview, no confusing setup or extra steps.
- The interview itself felt very realistic. It picked up on my background and asked me questions based on my actual experience, not random scenarios that don’t match my profile.
- Overall, it gave me exactly what I was looking for: a proper, structured mock interview environment that forces you to think and respond like it’s the real thing.

**Cons**

- If you only use the “Standard Interviewer” on the trial, you don’t fully experience the variety of interviewers and scenarios.
- Might feel like “overkill” if someone just wants a few quick questions instead of a full mock interview experience.

**Pros**

- Simple and easy to get started with, no complex onboarding or decisions to make.
- Good for revisiting fundamentals: the resources like “Machine Learning Basics for Developers”, “Crash Course”, and “Course Modules” can be decent if your basics are weak.
- Works more like a curated learning path; useful if someone is still early in their journey and needs foundational concepts.

**Cons**

- Doesn’t feel like an interview tool at all if you’re looking for **mock interviews** or role-specific practice.
- Very limited customization: you can’t properly specify your niche, target role, or interview format.
- Sends you into generic learning resources instead of simulating a real interview conversation.
- If you’ve already done courses and LeetCode/DSA/system design, it doesn’t really add anything new for interview-day prep.

Honestly, I wasn’t looking for any of the options; I wanted to have an interview in a realistic environment.

But if you really have friends with whom you can practice, or if you are comfortable practicing with peers, or want to fix a call with a FAANG expert, you can try Exponent.

For me, this wasn’t what I was looking for.

**Pros**

- Offers multiple ways to practice: with a friend, with peers, or with an expert , great if you like human-to-human mock interviews.
- Has dedicated tracks like “Data Structures”, “System Design”, “Product Management”, etc., so it’s structured around popular interview areas.
- The “expert mock interview” option can be useful if someone wants direct feedback from someone with FAANG-level experience.

**Cons**

- The flow is confusing: you click “Pramp”, land on Exponent, sign in, click again , not a smooth experience.
- All three options (friend / peers / expert) require other people or scheduling, which is not ideal if you specifically want _AI-based_, on-demand practice.
- Doesn’t give you that private, pressure-simulated environment where you can repeatedly mess up, refine, and re-try without involving another person.
- For someone like you who wanted an **AI interviewer** that feels like a real interview, this just didn’t match the expectation.

## 4\. Interviews Chat

Interview chat is simply and straightforwardly an Interview prep tool, no ifs and buts.

The dashboard has two options: “Interview Prep” and “AI interview Copilot”

With an Avatar having bad lip sync and a question, I don’t know how this is useful

**Pros**

- Very clearly positioned as an interview prep tool, no confusion about what it’s supposed to do.
- Dashboard is focused: “Interview Prep” and “AI Interview Copilot” makes the navigation straightforward.
- Uses both your resume and the job description, which is a good idea in theory for tailoring questions to your profile.

**Cons**

- Resume input is inconvenient: having to manually copy and paste your entire resume is clunky and a big friction point.
- The avatar experience isn’t polished , bad lip sync makes it feel more gimmicky than helpful, and can pull you _out_ of the interview mindset.
- The value of the avatar isn’t clear: you see a face move and a question, but it doesn’t necessarily translate into better feedback or a stronger interview simulation.
- Overall, it feels more like a “cool AI demo” than a tool that truly fixes the problem of communication under stress.

## 5\. Pramp

When I went on to the Pramp website and clicked on “Start Practising for free”, it took me to the exponent website.

There were a few options like “practice with peers” and “practice with AI”, so I chose the second one since that was my main purpose was to practice with AI

honestly exponent is not the best tool for interview practice either, if you want a real interview like experience.

Because as you can see in the image it gives you question and want you to answer it out loud and then submit it, this doesn’t happen in the real interviews. It definitely gives you a space to write and run code, people can try it out, but for me it was not the best fit.

## 5\. Lockedin AI

Next in line was Lockedin AI, they had so many tools, named as “Interview and meeting”, “coding”, “Online Assessment”, It was confusing for me to understand instantly which tool would help me with the mock interview. So I went with an online assessment, I clicked on “start for free”.

Press enter or click to view image in full size

![](https://miro.medium.com/v2/resize:fit:700/1*aNzbG79Rd3tcfRf7Q_0ZSA.png)

There were three options I could see: “Live, Mock, Coding”. I went with mock, and then there were a few options that we needed to fill in “Company, position and objective”.

Then I clicked on “Start Stimulator”

Press enter or click to view image in full size

![](https://miro.medium.com/v2/resize:fit:700/1*0EMw2Paifyey87avydD-xA.png)

I didn’t understand why I was the interviewer, the “hi” that you see, I sent that, I mean I didn’t know what to do next, and I didn’t have a lot of time to go through each and every feature. A tool should be straightforward in terms of navigation and direction. This tool might be good or not, who knows, but it definitely didn’t work for me. I didn’t try the tool even further because I knew it didn’t have what I wanted.

Press enter or click to view image in full size

![](https://miro.medium.com/v2/resize:fit:700/1*8ZPuMFjRPBK_NvIbKG48Aw.png)

**Pros**

- They clearly offer a lot of stuff , “Interview and meeting”, “Coding”, “Online Assessment”, so I’m sure there _is_ depth in the product somewhere.
- When I picked “Mock” under Online Assessment, it did ask for details like company, position, and objective, which means in theory it could create a more tailored experience if you’re willing to explore it properly.
- If someone has time and patience to click around and learn how it works, they might find a flow that fits them.

**Cons**

- The number of tools and labels actually made it harder to figure out where to start. I just wanted “mock interview with AI”, not a maze of options.
- Even after I chose “Mock” and clicked “Start Simulator”, the experience was confusing, suddenly I was the one acting like the interviewer, and I genuinely didn’t know what I was supposed to do next.
- The UX didn’t guide me at all. When you’re already stressed about interviews, you don’t want to sit and decode how a tool works.
- I didn’t have the time (or energy) to explore every feature just to see if it _might_ match what I needed.
- So honestly, I dropped it pretty quickly. Maybe it’s good, maybe it’s not, but for me, it failed the basic test: it wasn’t straightforward, and it didn’t give me the real interview-like experience I was actually looking for.

At the end of trying all these tools, I realised most of them were either learning platforms, peer-practice setups, or confusing dashboards that didn’t really feel like a real interview. I wasn’t looking for more theory or another course; I wanted something that would actually put me in the hot seat and test how I speak under pressure.

From my experience, FinalRound AI is an AI mock interview tool that actually feels like a real interview, with realistic interviewer avatars and questions that are tailored to my background and the role I’m preparing for.

Out of everything I tried, this was the only tool that genuinely felt like sitting in front of an actual interviewer, not just a screen. This review might sound biased, but Final Round AI actually delivered what it promised in my eyes. But in the end, it is totally up to you what environment or which type is interview simulation you need for your interview practice.

## Frequently Asked Questions  about Big Interview

How do I know it will work for me?

We know Big Interview works because we’ve tested and refined our platform with hundreds of thousands of job seekers before you. And our statistics clearly show that Big Interview is effective. Our users get a job after 4.5 weeks on average. That’s almost 5x faster than the current US average of 22.6 weeks. How have we achieved this? In short — all thanks to the expertise of our co-founder and chief coach, Pamela Skillings.

In addition to developing Big Interview, Pamela Skillings spent 12 years in executive-level marketing and human resources jobs for Fortune 500 companies (including Morgan Stanley, MasterCard International, and Citigroup). Pamela also still works with corporate and government clients to develop training, retention, communications, and recruiting programs. Clients include Citigroup, American Express, Ernst & Young, and the City of New York. Pamela’s work with corporations keeps her up to date on hiring trends and the employer perspective, which helps inform her coaching work with job seekers.

I don’t think I have enough time. How long does it take?

If you have 2 hours to spare, Big Interview will give you enough value to make you feel prepared for the upcoming interview. We have a special “Fast-Track” module designed specifically for people who need to prepare NOW. If you’re pressed for time, use the “Interview Practice” tool — you’ll get immediate feedback on your interview answers and plenty of insights along the way. Plus, great sample answers to common questions you can get inspired by.

Why do I need to prepare for my interview? Can’t I just be myself?

Sadly, it doesn’t work like that. Almost 50% of candidates fail the interview because they didn’t know how to properly research the company. Two out of three candidates struggle to make eye contact with the interviewer. 39% of candidates get rejected because of poor body language. We could go on and on with the stats. Truth is — interviewing for jobs is uncomfortable and difficult, solely because no one ever taught you how to do it. With Big Interview, you gain invaluable knowledge almost no other candidate has. With preparation, you’ll get an edge over 9 out of 10 other applicants who believe they simply “got this.”

How long will I need to use Big Interview for to see results?

You’ll get a huge boost to your interviewing skills within hours. But, obviously, the more work you put in, the better results you can expect. Big Interview is not just about interviewing. Inside our app, you’ll find lessons on salary negotiation, a resume writing course, a professional resume builder that helps you highlight your assets, and tips on how to find better jobs. And it doesn’t end when you do land that job. Our platform teaches you how to make the most of your career, get an internal promotion, go for that first managerial job, or even switch industries later in your career. That’s why one of our plans is lifetime access. Big Interview can become your ultimate career toolbox and help you navigate through all the challenges your professional life may throw at you.

How much does it cost? Can I afford it?

One-month access to Big Interview costs $39. A three-month plan is $99. Lifetime access — $299. And again, to put that into perspective — Big Interview typically helps you shave around 4 months off of your job search. That’s 4 fewer months of not getting your salary, and 4 fewer months of constant stress and anxiety. And if you’re still not sure if Big Interview is worth your investment, just give it a try. If you don’t think it’s worth what you’re paying, we’re offering you a 30-day money-back guarantee. No questions asked.
